# Use plain language and one thing per page

Write settings, onboarding, and forms in plain language, and ask one question or make one decision per page or step.

## Why

External standard, not learned from the user's feedback. Plain words and one decision at a time reduce errors and make each step easy to understand, answer, and recover.

## Prefer

- Use short sentences and everyday words.
- Give each onboarding step or form page one question or decision.
- Explain a setting by its effect, next to the setting.

## Avoid

- Long pages of mixed settings and questions.
- Jargon or internal names in settings and onboarding.

## Use when

- Designing onboarding, multi-step forms, or settings explanations.

## Do not use when

- Experts compare many related settings at once; a dense, well-grouped page serves them better.

## Sources

- GOV.UK Design System: Patterns — https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/
- GOV.UK Service Manual: Structuring forms (one thing per page) — https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/design/form-structure

## Check

- Could a new user understand every word?
- Does each step ask one thing?
- Is each setting explained by its effect?
